August 7, 2026

Ambetter of North Carolina, Inc.  
Attn: Member Appeals  
1701 North Graham Street, Suite 101  
Charlotte, NC 28206

Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Jordan Foster  
Member ID: W794852405  
Reference number: POC-EE22487639-86426  
Requested service: Lumbar disc decompression/discectomy  
CPT code: 63030  
Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Ambetter Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the requested lower-back disc surgery/decompression, CPT 63030. The denial states that the clinical records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. The records submitted with the authorization request do document extensive, appropriate, and unsuccessful conservative treatment.

The following information directly addresses the stated reason for denial:

- I have experienced 12 months of progressive lower-back pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy from May 3, 2026, through July 12, 2026, including 16 visits. Treatment included core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility exercises. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this course.
- I used NSAIDs for approximately six months, with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on June 9, 2026. It provided only approximately three weeks of partial relief, demonstrating that the intervention was temporary and insufficient.
- Despite these measures, I continue to have significant symptoms and functional impairment. I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and have radicular pain extending into my right calf.
- A lumbar MRI performed on June 28, 2026, showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the MRI abnormality.

These records establish that conservative treatment was not merely attempted briefly; it was performed over an adequate period and included supervised physical therapy, medication therapy, and an injection. The treatment failed to provide durable relief. The MRI and examination also establish an anatomic lesion and corresponding clinical findings explaining the persistent radicular symptoms and functional limitation.

There are no documented factors in the submitted records that would otherwise prevent surgery: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, the BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

For clarity, I am presenting the medical argument in my own words and am not quoting the plan’s policy language. Please identify the exact policy revision and any other clinical-review criteria used in this determination, including the specific records Ambetter believes were missing or insufficient. If Ambetter relied on criteria not included in the publicly available clinical-policy materials, please provide those criteria and the applicable revision or effective date.

I request that Ambetter:

1. Overturn the denial;
2. Approve prior authorization for CPT 63030 as recommended by Reyes, MD;
3. Conduct a complete review of the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection response, MRI report, and examination findings listed above; and
4. Provide a written explanation if the request remains denied, identifying precisely why the documented 10-week, 16-visit supervised physical-therapy course, six months of NSAID use, and corticosteroid injection are considered insufficient.

Please treat this letter and the enclosed clinical records as my formal member appeal. Please confirm receipt and provide the appeal case number and expected decision date.

Sincerely,

Jordan Foster  
Member ID: W794852405

Enclosures:

- Adverse Benefit Determination dated August 7, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note
- Physical therapy treatment records
- Medication history
- Corticosteroid injection record dated June 9, 2026
- Lumbar MRI report dated June 28, 2026
- Relevant examination records
- Surgical recommendation from Reyes, MD
